_comment: Instantly campaign definition for the VisioneerIT reach-engine pilot. NOT YET CREATED in Instantly - no campaign id exists yet; the parent agent creates it there from this file. Built to the same rules as campaign-oryoniq-pilot.json and checked by hand against n8n-workflows/sync-routes.py's check_instantly_copy and check_cta_sentence (note: sync-routes.py's CAMPAIGNS map does not list this file yet, so running the script today reports 'no Instantly campaign file yet - nothing to check' for visioneerit rather than actively validating it; wiring that in is a separate change to sync-routes.py, which this task does not own). {{personalization}} is filled per-lead from the engine's opener; {{sendrPageUrl}} is the lead's own Sendr page, supplied per-lead as a TOP-LEVEL custom_variable (nested inside `payload` it is silently discarded and the API still returns 201). 4-step sequence landing roughly day 0 / 3 / 7 / 13, same cadence as the OryonIQ pilot. BLOCK ORDER in step 1 is greeting / {{personalization}} / offer / ask / page link / sign-off, matching the OryonIQ file: the ask sits BEFORE the link on purpose, as the real call to action, with the page as the lower-commitment alternative. The two step-1 variants share their CTA sentence AND their ask, word for word, and differ ONLY in the offer paragraph - that is the A/B question: variant A states plainly what VisioneerIT does (the config's `offer`, verbatim), variant B leads with 'the architecture is not what usually slips, the timeline does' and arrives at the same offer from the risk side. Testing more than one change at once would tell us nothing about which one moved the number. Steps 2-4 subjects are deliberately EMPTY so the follow-ups thread under step 1. Every step signs off with the config's `sender` (Ellen / VisioneerIT). TRUTH CONSTRAINT observed throughout: VisioneerIT sells zero-trust architecture, AI-assisted security operations, and CMMC readiness to federal and SLED agencies - nothing here claims a specific customer, certification, contract vehicle, metric, or a 'free tier' (unlike OryonIQ, VisioneerIT is not known to have one, so step 4 closes on the contact page instead of inventing a no-cost offer). The September 30, 2027 DoD zero-trust deadline in config-visioneerit.json's `signal` is DoD-specific, not universal across every federal/SLED recipient, so no step asserts that exact date applies to the reader's own organization - the copy asks about 'zero-trust and CMMC readiness' generally instead of naming the deadline as theirs. COMPLIANCE FOOTER added 2026-08-30 to every step: a valid physical postal address and an opt-out, both required by CAN-SPAM 7704(a)(5) and absent from all 10 bodies until now. The opt-out is reply-based, not a merge tag, because the reply route is already wired to the Suppression tab and proven, while an unverified tag can reach a prospect as a literal token.
